tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search live jobs on the 27 Locate Jobs Network job boards: Diversity Careers, Healthcare Jobs for Veterans, Nature Jobs, University Fundraising Jobs, Fiber Optic Jobs, Certified Medical Assistant Jobs, Forklift Jobs, HR Analyst Jobs, The Trades Jobs, IT Jobs, Optometry Jobs, Dentist Jobs, Funeral Service Jobs, Chiropractor Jobs, Veterinarian Jobs, SLP Jobs, Diversity Higher Education Jobs, Minority Finance Jobs, Bioinformatics Jobs, Minority Jobs, Physical Therapist Jobs, Nurse Practitioner Jobs, Arborist Jobs, Social Worker Jobs, Paralegal Careers, LPN Jobs, and Medical Lab Jobs. Search by role or skill, by place (a city and state, a state, or a ZIP code, which searches its whole state), or for remote jobs. Returns 5 to 10 current jobs with title, employer, location, posted date, and a link to the job page on the board that lists it, plus a link to see more. It only reads job listings: it cannot apply for a job, post a job, or save a search.

what.description: The role or skill, such as "dental hygienist", "forklift", or "payroll". Every word must appear in the job title or the employer's name, so keep it to the words a title uses ("help desk", not "IT help desk support role"). Leave out to list the newest jobs.

where.description: A city with its state ("Columbus, OH"), a state, a ZIP code (searches its whole state), or "remote". Leave out for the whole U.S.

limit.description: How many jobs to return, 5 to 10. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: unemployment_answers
tools.description: A checked answer about unemployment benefits for a U.S. state, covering Alabama, Arizona, Idaho, Indiana, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, and Utah. Give a state (a name or 2-letter code) and either a topic or the person's own question; the tool picks the topic from the question when none is given. For a state we do not cover yet, it names the federal page that finds that state's own unemployment office instead of guessing at a figure. It only reads a checked guide: it cannot file a claim, check a claim's status, or change anyone's benefits.

state.description: A U.S. state, by name or 2-letter code, such as "Texas" or "TX".

topic.description: One of the 13 topics: "home" (An overview: how to apply and what it pays.), "eligibility" (Who qualifies for unemployment benefits.), "apply" (How to file an unemployment claim.), "amounts" (How much it pays each week.), "duration" (How many weeks benefits last.), "weekly-claims" (Requesting payment and work search each week.), "jobs" (The state's own job search and job bank.), "appeals" (Denials, appeals, and overpayments.), "taxes" (How unemployment benefits are taxed.), "disability" (Disability benefits (SSDI, SSI) and how they relate to unemployment.), "offices" (The agency's offices and phone numbers.), "contact" (Who to contact about a specific claim.), "faq" (Common questions that cross several topics.). Leave out to pick the topic from the question instead.

question.description: The person's own question, used to pick a topic when none is given.
